abstract:
<jats:sec xml:lang="en">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p xml:lang="en">
                      We aim to evaluate the association of within‐individual changes in consumption of total and specific types of nuts and the subsequent risk of incident cardiovascular disease (
                      <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">CVD</jats:styled-content>
                      ) in
                      <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">US</jats:styled-content>
                      men and women.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec xml:lang="en">
                    <jats:title>Methods and Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p xml:lang="en">
                      We included 34 103 men from the HPFS (Health Professionals Follow‐Up Study) (1986–2012), 77 815 women from the NHS (Nurses’ Health Study) (1986–2012), and 80 737 women from the NHS
                      <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">II</jats:styled-content>
                      (1991–2013). We assessed nut consumption every 4 years using validated food frequency questionnaires. We used multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression models to examine the association between 4‐year changes in nut consumption and risk of confirmed
                      <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">CVD</jats:styled-content>
                      end points in the subsequent 4 years. Per 0.5 serving/day increase in total nut consumption was associated with lower risk of
                      <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">CVD</jats:styled-content>
                      (relative risk [RR], 0.92; 95%
                      <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">CI</jats:styled-content>
                      , 0.86–0.98), coronary heart disease (RR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.89–0.99), and stroke (RR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.83–0.95). Compared with individuals who remained nonconsumers in a 4‐year interval, those who had higher consumption of total nuts (≥0.5 servings/day) had a lower risk of
                      <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">CVD</jats:styled-content>
                      (RR, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.67–0.84), coronary heart disease (RR, 0.80; 95% CI, 0.69–0.93), and stroke (RR, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.57–0.82) in next 4 years. Individuals who decreased nut consumption by ≥0.50 servings/day had a higher risk of developing
                      <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">CVD</jats:styled-content>
                      (RR, 1.14; 95% CI, 0.99–1.32), coronary heart disease (RR, 1.06; 95% CI, 0.88–1.28), and stroke (RR, 1.28; 95% CI, 1.02–1.60) when compared with those who maintained their nut consumption.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec xml:lang="en">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p xml:lang="en">
                      Increasing total consumption of nuts and intake of individual types of nuts (eg, walnuts, other tree nuts, and peanuts) was associated with a subsequent lower risk of
                      <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">CVD</jats:styled-content>
                      . These data support the role of nut intake in the primary prevention of
                      <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">CVD</jats:styled-content>
                      .
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec xml:lang="en">
                    <jats:title>Registration</jats:title>
                    <jats:p xml:lang="en">
                      <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">URL</jats:styled-content>
                      :
                      <jats:ext-link xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" ext-link-type="uri" xlink:href="http://www.clinicaltrials.gov">http://www.clini​caltr​ials.gov</jats:ext-link>
                      . Unique identifiers:
                      <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">NCT</jats:styled-content>
                      00005152 and
                      <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">NCT</jats:styled-content>
                      00005182.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
